14	CASE OD2-DEV-KNOWN (KNOWN, organizational): Tallowmere Mutual: property claims turnaround doubles
15	Setting: Tallowmere Mutual is a fictional regional insurer. Its Personal Lines Property Claims unit in Dunmore has 24 adjusters, three team leads and one claims manager, and reports to VP Claims Graham Ostrowe. The unit settles about 1,400 claims a month. The time from first notice of loss to settlement decision used to be just under 10 days. From April it rose and has stayed near 18 days through August. During the same months the unit switched document-imaging providers, handled a hail catastrophe, lost two senior adjusters, and closed an internal audit action.
16	Presenting request: The COO writes: 'Graham wants four contract adjusters through year-end and wants to start talks about moving back to our old imaging provider. Before I sign anything, tell me why our claims turnaround doubled and what we should actually do about it.'
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Claims operations dashboard, monthly extract (system-record): Personal Lines Property – mean days from first notice of loss to settlement decision, all closed claims. Jan 9.6 | Feb 9.5 | Mar 9.9 | Apr 14.2 | May 17.6 | Jun 18.1 | Jul 17.8 | Aug 18.2. Unit target: 10.0. Dashboard annotations: '17 Mar – document imaging cutover to Quillfast'; '14–16 Apr – CAT-0414 hail event declared'. Status: RED since April.
19	E2 [stage S1] Email, Graham Ostrowe (VP Claims) to COO, 4 September (leadership-account): Turnaround is a capacity story, plain and simple. CAT-0414 dumped nearly 600 extra claims on us in April. Before we had dug out, we lost Alan Pryce and Joyce Mbeki, our two most senior adjusters, in May. On top of that, the Quillfast imaging switch has been rough, and adjusters tell me documents are slow to show up. I'm asking you to approve four contract adjusters through year-end, and I'd like Procurement to open talks on moving back to our previous imaging provider. Give me the people and I expect us back under 10 days by November.
20	E3 [stage S1] HR headcount record, Property Claims, Jan–Aug (system-record): Resignations: A. Pryce, Senior Adjuster, last day 9 May; J. Mbeki, Senior Adjuster, last day 23 May. Backfill: two contract adjusters (Halvern Staffing) started 2 June and carried full caseloads from 16 June. Adjuster FTE: Jan–Apr 24; mid-May 23; late May 22; Jun–Aug 24. Team leads: 3, no change. Claims manager: 1, no change. No other leavers or long-term absences recorded.
21	E4 [stage S1] July pulse survey, Property Claims (31 of 38 staff responded) (anonymous-staff-survey): Question: 'What is the biggest obstacle to closing claims quickly?' Coded themes: imaging/document retrieval 9; workload since the storm 8; waiting on other people 7; systems/IT 4; other 3. Selected verbatims: 'Quillfast viewer is clunky – three clicks to find one photo.' 'Still feels like we never recovered from the hail.' 'Half my files sit in someone else's tray waiting for a signature.' 'The contractors are good but still need hand-holding.'
22	E5 [stage S1] Complaints register summary, Property Claims (system-record): Formal complaints logged: Jan 29 | Feb 33 | Mar 31 | Apr 58 | May 71 | Jun 76 | Jul 72 | Aug 74. Most frequent category Jun–Aug: 'Delay', coded on 41% of complaints. Register note: a new complaints module went live on 1 April. From that date, broker telephone complaints are logged as formal complaints, and the 'Delay' category was created. Before April, delay-related complaints were coded 'Service – other'.
23	E6 [stage S1] Claims operations management meeting minutes, 3 April (document): Present: G. Ostrowe, claims manager, team leads D. Fell, M. Oyelaran, R. Kimball, ops analyst. 1. Quillfast cutover complete 17 Mar. Indexing outage 24–25 Mar now resolved. 2. Spring storm readiness: CAT staffing roster agreed. 3. Audit action CLM-26-03 closed: revised DAM live 1 Apr; adjusters briefed 28 Mar. 4. Team leads report tray volumes up this week. GO: 'should settle once people adjust; revisit in May.' 5. AOB: summer leave planning.
24	CATALOGUE (full contents)
25	C1 [stage S1] Monthly new-claim registrations and open inventory, Jan–Aug - Claims platform volume report (system-record): New claims registered: Jan 1,402 | Feb 1,381 | Mar 1,428 | Apr 1,987 | May 1,566 | Jun 1,409 | Jul 1,388 | Aug 1,415. CAT-0414-coded registrations: Apr 571, May 96, Jun 8, Jul 0, Aug 0. Open claim inventory at month end: Jan 448 | Feb 452 | Mar 455 | Apr 1,010 | May 905 | Jun 852 | Jul 848 | Aug 860.
26	C2 [stage S1] Claim status-history extract by settlement value band, Q1 vs Jun–Aug - Claims platform status-history extract, ops analyst (system-record): Closed property claims, mean days per stage by final settlement band. Format: Q1 (Jan–Mar) → Jun–Aug. Under $2,500 (39% → 38% of closures): intake/indexing 0.8 → 0.9; adjuster investigation 3.5 → 3.6; pending authority approval 0.1 → 0.1; payment issue 1.7 → 1.7; total 6.1 → 6.3. $2,500–$10,000 (52% → 53%): intake/indexing 0.9 → 1.0; investigation 6.9 → 7.0; pending authority approval 0.7 → 16.0; payment issue 1.9 → 2.0; total 10.4 → 26.0. Over $10,000 (9% → 9%): intake/indexing 1.0 → 1.0; investigation 12.8 → 13.1; pending approval (claims manager) 5.3 → 5.4; payment issue 1.9 → 2.0; total 21.0 → 21.5. 'Pending authority approval' runs from the adjuster's settlement recommendation to approver sign-off.
27	C3 [stage S1] Adjuster active caseload and overtime report, Jan–Aug - Claims workforce management report (system-record): Mean active claims per adjuster, excluding claims awaiting approval: Jan 17.0 | Feb 17.2 | Mar 17.1 | Apr 24.8 | May 19.9 | Jun 17.4 | Jul 16.9 | Aug 17.0. Mean adjuster overtime, hours/week: Q1 1.0; Apr 5.2; May 2.6; Jun–Aug 1.1. Contract adjusters were assigned 85% of a standard caseload from 16 June. Quality-review pass rate on adjuster files: Q1 94%, Jun–Aug 93%.
28	C4 [stage S1] Document indexing service logs, legacy provider and Quillfast, Jan–Aug - Quillfast and legacy provider indexing logs, compiled by IT (log): Median time from document receipt to indexed-and-viewable in the claim file: legacy provider Jan–16 Mar 5.2 hours; Quillfast 17 Mar–31 Aug 3.9 hours. 95th percentile: legacy 14 hours; Quillfast 11 hours. Incident: 24–25 March, 31-hour Quillfast outage, 1,140 documents delayed, backlog cleared 26 March. No other outages over 1 hour. Viewer page-load errors recorded by the claims platform: 0.4% of sessions.
29	C5 [stage S1] Internal Audit report IA-26-03 and change record CR-0331 - Internal Audit report (issued 12 Feb) and claims change register (change-record): IA-26-03 finding, rated High: 17 of 120 sampled settlements between $2,500 and $10,000 from last year's second half contained overpayments (mean $730) and had no second review. Agreed management action: as an interim control, cut adjuster settlement authority to $2,500 from 1 April; team leads approve settlements of $2,500–$10,000; the over-$10,000 route to the claims manager stays the same. Audit will re-test Q2–Q3 settlements in December. Permanent thresholds and any related resourcing are to be set only after that re-test. CR-0331, approved 20 Mar by G. Ostrowe: 'Delegated authority matrix (DAM) revision per IA-26-03. Affected roles: adjusters, team leads. Workload impact assessment: not performed – expected minimal.'
30	C6 [stage S1] Team-lead approval tray report, weekly, Jan–Aug - Claims platform workflow report, three team leads combined (system-record): Items routed to team-lead trays per week: Q1 average 38 (coverage exceptions, ex-gratia requests). Tray depth at week end: 3 Apr 11; 10 Apr 52; 1 May 268; 29 May 287; 31 Jul 412; 28 Aug 455. Team-lead logged overtime: Q1 0.8 h/week each; Jun–Aug 6.4 h/week each. Other team-lead duties (coaching, complaint escalations, CAT reserve reviews) unchanged in scope.
31	C7 [stage S1] Finance note on paid severity, $2,500–$10,000 band, Q1 vs Jun–Aug - Claims finance analyst note, 5 September (financial-record): Average paid amount, $2,500–$10,000 band: Q1 $5,610; Jun–Aug $5,370 (−4.3%). 32	C8 [stage S1] Complaints team note on Jun–Aug complaint sources and coding - Customer complaints team lead, note dated 9 September (document): Of 222 formal complaints in Jun–Aug, 64 came from broker telephone calls. The logging agent assigns categories from free text, and there is no quality check on coding. Several complaints coded 'Delay' also cite a coverage decision. We cannot produce a like-for-like series against pre-April data.
33	C9 [stage S1] Learning and training records, claims unit, Jan–Aug - Learning management system export (system-record): Annual fraud-awareness module: 100% of adjusters completed by 30 April. Quillfast viewer training: 6 adjusters attended in March, and a recorded session is available to all. Contract adjuster induction: 3 days, 2–4 June. Team-lead coaching skills workshop: half day, 14 May, all three team leads. No other mandatory training due in the period.
34	C10 [stage S1] Post-settlement customer satisfaction survey results, Q1 and Q2 - Customer experience team, quarterly survey (customer-account): Post-settlement satisfaction (1–5 scale): Q1 4.1 (n=412); Q2 3.7 (n=455). Share of comments mentioning speed or waiting: Q1 12%; Q2 29%. Sample comments: 'Took weeks to hear anything after the adjuster visited.' 'Adjuster was lovely, the process was slow.' 'Hail damage settled fairly in the end.' The survey does not record settlement value or claim type.
35	C11 [stage S1] IT service desk tickets tagged Claims Platform, Mar–Aug - IT service management export (log): 212 tickets. Categories: password/access 71; printer and mail merge 38; Quillfast viewer display issues 29; slow screen response 17; report requests 22; other 35. Median resolution 0.6 business days. No priority-1 incidents other than the 24–25 March Quillfast outage. Ticket volume by month: Mar 49, Apr 37, May 33, Jun 31, Jul 30, Aug 32.
36	C12 [stage S1] Statement from Quillfast account manager on service performance - Letter from Quillfast account manager to Tallowmere Procurement, 8 September (vendor-account): We are aware of concerns raised internally at Tallowmere. Apart from the March incident, for which we have issued a service credit, Quillfast has met or beaten every contractual indexing service level every month. We would welcome a workshop with your adjusters to configure viewer shortcuts. A move back to your previous provider would incur early-termination charges under clause 14.2.
37	CANDIDATES
38	H1: The 1 April revision of the delegated settlement authority matrix is the main cause of the sustained rise in turnaround. It routes $2,500–$10,000 settlements to three team leads, who cannot keep up with the approvals.
39	H2: The claim surge from the April CAT-0414 hail event is the main driver of turnaround staying near 18 days through June–August.
40	H3: The May loss of two senior adjusters reduced adjuster capacity and is the main driver of the turnaround increase.
41	H4: The March switch to Quillfast document imaging is delaying claim files and is a main driver of the turnaround increase.
42	H5: The interim $2,500 adjuster authority limit is reducing overpayments on $2,500–$10,000 settlements.
43	R1: Adjuster settlement authority cut from $10,000 to $2,500 on 1 April -> Increase in the time $2,500–$10,000 claims spend pending authority approval (causes)
44	R2: CAT-0414 hail-event claim surge in April -> Turnaround staying near 18 days through June–August (causes)
45	R3: Longer claim turnaround -> Rise in formal complaints logged from April (causes)
46	R4: May departures of two senior adjusters -> Longer adjuster investigation stage on claims (causes)
47	A1: With Internal Audit, add interim approval capacity for the $2,500–$10,000 band, for example by certifying experienced senior adjusters as second approvers or temporarily moving other team-lead duties elsewhere. Keep a second review on every claim in the band, and track time pending approval weekly.
48	A2: Immediately restore adjusters' sole settlement authority to $10,000 to clear the approval tray, without waiting for Internal Audit.
49	A3: Put the three team leads on performance improvement plans for slow settlement approvals.
50	A4: Make the $2,500 adjuster limit the permanent authority standard now, and fund a fourth team-lead post dedicated to approvals.
51	SCORED ITEMS
52	S-H1: hypothesis H1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
53	S-H2: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
54	S-H3: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
55	S-H4: hypothesis H4 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
56	S-H5: hypothesis H5 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
57	S-R1: edge R1 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
58	S-R2: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
59	S-R3: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
60	S-R4: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
61	S-A1: action A1 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
62	S-A2: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
63	S-A3: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
64	S-A4: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
65	S-SUFF: sufficiency SUFF allowed=[sufficient, insufficient]
